title: Pakistan's biggest military shake-up puts nuclear command under Asim Munir: What it means
summary: Pakistan has restructured its defence command with the 27th Constitutional Amendment to create a National Strategic Command that centralises operational control of strategic assets, including the nuclear arsenal. Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir leads the overhaul, and Lieutenant General Syed Aamer Raza has been named the first commander. The move shifts authority away from the civilian-led National Command Authority and mirrors a China-style command model backed by the Strategic Plans Division.
content:
Pakistan has initiated a major restructuring of its defence architecture through the 27th Constitutional Amendment, introducing a new command structure that centralises operational control of the country’s strategic assets under the military.

According to reporting cited by Moneycontrol and CNN-News18, the newly created National Strategic Command will oversee Pakistan’s strategic capabilities, including its nuclear arsenal. The change marks a significant shift from the existing civilian-led National Command Authority framework, with the prime minister’s role described as informational rather than operational.

The restructuring is being led by Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, who is serving in the dual roles of Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff. Lieutenant General Syed Aamer Raza, formerly the Chief of the General Staff, has been promoted to four-star general and appointed as the first Commander of the National Strategic Command.

Observers note that the NSC’s organisational model closely resembles elements of China’s People’s Liberation Army, particularly the PLA Rocket Force. Backed by the Strategic Plans Division, the new command consolidates management of nuclear stockpiles, missile systems, delivery platforms and strategic weapons development under a single authority.

The intent of the reorganisation is to create an integrated operational command bringing together the Army, Navy, Air Force, Rocket Force and Strategic Command. Officials cited in reports say the objective is to strengthen strategic deterrence along Pakistan’s eastern border and to expand defence-industrial and technological cooperation with Beijing.

The shake-up has also reshaped internal military functioning. Promotion boards for senior officers have reportedly been on hold for more than 15 months as the armed forces reorganise the command structure. Routine Formation Commanders’ Conferences have been suspended since 2024, a sign analysts say of greater centralisation of decision-making within the top military leadership.

Reports further indicate that operational authority has increasingly been consolidated under the Office of the Chief of Defence Forces, reducing the traditional autonomy exercised by regional corps commanders. The consolidation of strategic control raises questions about civil-military relations in Pakistan and has implications for regional security dynamics.

The changes will be closely watched by international partners and regional neighbours given Pakistan’s strategic position and nuclear capabilities. Officials and analysts will likely monitor how the new command affects command-and-control procedures, deterrence posture, and cooperation with foreign defence partners.

According to a CNN-News18 report, the newly created National Strategic Command (NSC) will oversee Pakistan's strategic capabilities, including its nuclear arsenal. The move marks a significant shift from the existing civilian-led National Command Authority (NCA) framework, with the prime minister's role reportedly becoming "strictly informational rather than operational."

The restructuring is being led by Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, who currently serves in the dual roles of Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff (COAS).

Lieutenant General Syed Aamer Raza, formerly the Chief of the General Staff, has been promoted to the rank of four-star general and appointed as the first Commander of the National Strategic Command, the report said.

China-inspired command model

The report said the NSC's organisational structure closely resembles that of China's People's Liberation Army (PLA), particularly the PLA Rocket Force.

Backed by the Strategic Plans Division (SPD), the new command consolidates the management of nuclear stockpiles, missile systems, delivery platforms and strategic weapons development under a single authority.

The restructuring is intended to create an integrated operational command bringing together the Army, Navy, Air Force, Rocket Force and Strategic Command. According to the report, the objective is to strengthen strategic deterrence along Pakistan's eastern border while expanding defence-industrial and technological cooperation with Beijing.

Impact on Pakistan's military

The changes have also reshaped the internal functioning of Pakistan's armed forces. According to the report, promotion boards for senior officers have remained on hold for more than 15 months as the military reorganises its command structure.

Routine Formation Commanders' Conferences have reportedly been suspended since 2024, indicating greater centralisation of decision-making within the top military leadership.

The report also said operational authority has increasingly been consolidated under the Office of the Chief of Defence Forces, reducing the traditional autonomy exercised by regional Corps Commanders.
